Hi all — I reviewed the SOW and sketched three practical invoice/recognition patterns we commonly use. I attached an XLS sample with the numeric splits. TL;DR + recommended path for audit simplicity below.

Options:
- Option A — Annual slice invoices (recommended): Redwood issues 1 invoice per 12-month contract year. Payment can be captured up front or via scheduled invoices; we record deferred revenue on receipt and amortize ratably over each contract year (straight-line). Easiest for auditors.
- Option B — Cash-first single invoice, customer amortizes internally: Redwood issues a single upfront invoice; we provide an amortization certificate but do not split invoices. This keeps billing simple but adds work for the customer's accounting team.
- Option C — Escrow-backed partial surety (less common): Redwood allows a third-party escrow arrangement for the portion attributed to years 2–3. We require the escrow agreement to name Redwood as beneficiary for service failure, and legal sign-off. This may affect discounting and requires a custodial fee.

Recommended language for audit workpapers / vendor confirmation: "Redwood Inference will recognize revenue ratably over each 12‑month contract period. For prepayments received, deferred revenue is established on the date of receipt and amortized on a monthly basis over the covered period. Redwood will provide schedules and a certified invoice file on request for audit purposes."

A few practical notes:
- If ProspectCorp wants split invoices but will pay upfront with a single ACH, we can still generate separate invoice documents (one per year) and apply the single payment across them.
- If escrow is requested, expect ~30–45 day legal turnaround; the escrow agent agreement needs to be standard. There may be a small set-up fee which we can estimate.

Attachments: Redwood_MultiYear_Invoice_Sample.xlsx (sample split scenarios, GL codes masked).

Marissa Cole
Head of Finance Operations, Redwood Inference

Oliver — looping back with our recommended approach and a commercial tweak to make escrow workable without changing the price materially. Proposed path: 

1) Billing: Redwood will issue three invoices (one per contract year) dated on contract start anniversary (we can backdate docs to match internal audit needs). You can remit as a single upfront payment; Finance will apply the payment across the three invoices.
2) Recognition: Redwood will put the full amount into deferred revenue on receipt and amortize monthly by invoice period. We will provide a certified amortization schedule for your auditors.
3) Escrow: We are open to a limited escrow for years 2–3 covering up to 50% of the value of year-2 and year-3 invoices. Terms: escrow with a recognized agent (example list attached), Redwood named beneficiary for service-failure claims, escrow release conditions tied to insolvency or breach only. To keep economics neutral we propose a nominal 1.5% fee passed to ProspectCorp (covers agent + admin).
4) Commercial / Discounting: Given the flexibility on escrow, our standard multi-year prepay discounts apply. If ProspectCorp requires full escrow without any administrative fee, we would need to reduce the discount by 2% to offset escrow costs.

Next steps — propose we:
- Confirm which option you prefer (A,B,C) — Oliver
- If escrow required, ProspectCorp to confirm preferred escrow agent and provide standard escrow template — ProspectCorp legal
- Ben to issue amendment + DocuSign (I’ve started a draft) — Ben

I will draft the amendment and a sample invoice sequence this afternoon and share the DocuSign link.

Thanks — Ben
